meaning: to delay or postpone doing something, often because you don't want to do it
nuance: Carries a hint of avoidance or reluctance that 'postpone' doesn't — you put off the dentist because you dread it, not just because of scheduling. Also has a separate sense: to make someone dislike or feel repelled by something.

confusables.difference: postpone is neutral and formal, used for scheduled events; put off suggests personal avoidance and works in casual speech
delay is often caused by external factors (traffic, weather); put off implies a choice to avoid something

examples: I keep putting off calling the dentist.
His rudeness put me off the whole idea of working there.
memory_hook: Picture pushing a task 'off' your desk into tomorrow's pile.
